contradictions.detail: The listing's vehicle-history summary states 'No Accident or Damage Reported'. The attached CARFAX (10/19/2026) reports an insurance TOTAL LOSS from collision on 08/03/2025 and front damage on 08/06/2025.
The listing headline says 'LikeNew UltraLowMiles' and leads with 'Clean Title - $4,000 Savings' while omitting that the car was declared an insurance total loss 14 months ago.

critical_evidence.evidence: The CARFAX has no reported service entries over 9.5 years, only DMV registrations. The listing provides no receipts. Brake fluid and oil-by-time are undocumented.
CARFAX shows manufacture on 04/12/2017, an early-2017 6MT build in the higher-risk window. No transmission repair or warranty records and no door-jamb build-date photo in the attached set.
RF hardtop, so soft-top fabric is not relevant, but the targa/rear drain areas and footwells still apply. No photos with carpet lifted or of drain areas examined here.

CARFAX says 'No open recalls reported', but the NHTSA list shows 24V695000 (airbag control module software, 2016-2023 MX-5) applies to this VIN, with no completion record. 19V072000 is automatic-only and does not apply to this manual. A dealer VIN printout is needed.
No tire, battery or service claims or receipts. Tread looks reasonable in the photos, but DOT and battery date codes were not examined here.

documentation.rationale: The identity/terms half is present: VIN, decode match, all-in dealer price, and a full CARFAX showing title and ownership. The maintenance half is absent: zero service entries, no receipts, no repair invoices for a collision total loss, and no photos of at-risk areas.

condition.rationale: Photos show a clean, straight-looking exterior, tidy black leather and a clean stock engine bay. Against that, the CARFAX establishes a collision total loss with front damage 14 months ago and no repair documentation, structural check or SRS scan. Visual cleanliness is not evidence of a correct repair.

price_value.rationale: The $21,450 ask sits inside the fair-value band ($20,495–$22,966, mid $21,636). That band is built on sold comps that are not insurance total-loss cars. A documented total loss typically carries a large resale discount, so the price is effectively above risk-adjusted value.

mission_fit.rationale: It meets the manual requirement, is within the $27,000 ceiling (above the ideal $19,000 band), and the ND is mechanically simple. The total-loss record directly undermines the 'easy to resell in 6-24 months' requirement, and the April 2017 build carries early-6MT gearbox risk.

logistics.rationale: Dealer in Louisville, KY, a long way from Carmel. Fly-and-drive is feasible, and a dealer lot should allow an independent or collision-shop PPI, but access is not stated. CA registration of an out-of-state car should be feasible with smog.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: RF Grand Touring with the 6-speed manual, gray over black/red-stitch leather, stock and low miles is a desirable spec. ND1 155 hp, not the ND2.

positives: RF Grand Touring with a 6-speed manual: the right transmission and a desirable, well-equipped trim (photo- and VIN-verified).

concerns: Observed: the CARFAX reports an insurance TOTAL LOSS (collision) on 08/03/2025 and front damage on 08/06/2025, while the listing claims 'No Accident or Damage Reported'. No repair invoices, damage photos or insurer estimate are provided.
Observed: chain of custody after the total loss is unexplained. The Indiana owner renewed registration 10/24/2025, and the car appears at a KY dealer 09/16/2026 with no reported title transfer.
Observed: no service entries of any kind in 9.5 years of CARFAX history. Time-based items (brake fluid, coolant age, fluids, battery, tires) are undocumented.
Unverified: early-2017 build (04/12/2017) 6MT, so no transmission history or build-date photo (inspect warm shifts into 2nd/3rd; ask for warranty records).
Unverified: airbag control module recall 24V695000 completion (ask for a Mazda dealer VIN printout); the SRS system is especially relevant after a front collision.
Unverified: tire DOT and battery dates; original 2017 tires are plausible at this mileage (photograph the date codes).

seller_questions: The CARFAX shows an insurance total loss on 08/03/2025 and front damage on 08/06/2025. Can you send the insurer's damage estimate and any pre-repair damage photos?
Where did you acquire the car (trade-in, owner buy-back, or Copart/IAA)? If auction, can you share the auction listing and its photos?

Was the front structure measured on a frame bench after repair? Is there a printout?

Can you provide a Mazda dealer VIN printout showing recall 24V695000 (airbag control module software) completed?
Can you send photos of the DOT date codes on all four tires and the battery date label?
Are there any oil-change or brake-fluid service records from the prior owner or from your reconditioning?
Can you send a cold-start video plus a scan-tool report showing no stored SRS, ABS or engine codes?
Will you allow an independent collision-repair specialist and a mechanic to inspect the car on a lift before any deposit?
Why was the listing tagged 'Clean Title - $4,000 Savings', and does the price already reflect the total-loss history?
ppi_focus: Collision-specialist inspection: frame-rail, radiator-support and crash-bar measurement; weld and sealer evidence; replaced-panel bolt marks.
Paint-depth readings on the aluminum hood, front fenders and front bumper; panel gaps at the headlamps and hood.
SRS/ABS/engine scan for stored codes; confirm airbag recall 24V695000 status and sensor function.
Radiator, A/C condenser, coolant hoses and the water-pump weep hole for post-collision leaks or non-OEM parts.
Adaptive LED headlamp function and aim; front suspension arms, tie rods and a full four-wheel alignment readout.
Warm road test of the early-2017 6MT: 2nd/3rd synchro grind, pop-out, clutch slip in 4th-6th, engagement point.
RF roof cycled several times: sensors, motor, rattles, targa seals and drain function; lift footwell carpet for moisture and seat-rail corrosion.
Tire DOT dates, battery date code, brake-fluid moisture test.
Underside check for diff pinion/output seal seepage and any collision-related damage to the subframe or undertray.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: insurer estimate and repair invoices showing a modest, cosmetic front repair with OEM parts, plus a clean collision-shop structural measurement and a clean SRS scan.
Up: price renegotiated to reflect total-loss resale stigma, well below the clean-history fair-value band.
Down: auction photos or invoices showing structural, crash-bar, radiator-support or airbag-sensor damage, or a dealer refusal of an independent PPI.
Down: grinding in 2nd/3rd when warm, or a stored SRS code.
evidence.mission_note: The spec suits the enthusiast bridge brief: manual RF, light, simple, inside the ceiling. The CARFAX total-loss record works directly against the resale-in-6-24-months part of the mission unless the price fully absorbs that stigma.
evidence.rationale: The attached CARFAX establishes a 2017 RF Grand Touring 6MT with one Indiana owner, 12,992 miles, and no DMV title brand. It also records an insurance total loss from collision on 08/03/2025 and front damage on 08/06/2025, which contradicts the listing's 'No Accident or Damage Reported' summary. No repair invoices, insurer estimate, structural measurement or SRS scan accompany the car. The chain of custody between the total loss and the KY dealer is unexplained. The CARFAX contains no service entries in 9.5 years, so time-based maintenance, the early-2017 gearbox history, recall 24V695000 closure, and tire and battery dates are all open. Photos show a clean, apparently stock exterior, interior and engine bay with even front panel fit, but photos cannot verify repair quality. The $21,450 ask sits inside a fair-value band derived from clean-history sales, which does not account for total-loss resale stigma.
evidence.next_action: Email the dealer asking for the insurer damage estimate, the acquisition source (with auction photos if applicable), itemized repair invoices, and written agreement to an independent collision-shop and mechanical PPI in Louisville before any deposit.
